subject: AuthZ change log retention and extract plan for SOC 2 / SIG review
message_1_subject: AuthZ change log retention and extract plan for SOC 2 / SIG review
message_1_body:
Hi Sean,

We’re working through the SIG and CAIQ questionnaire and have a follow-up on admin/change logs. Specifically we need: a) what fields you retain for authorization (role/grant/revoke) events, b) retention windows per event type, and c) how we can request a time-bounded extract for a compliance review.

Our deadline for the SIG upload is next Tuesday; can you confirm format and turnaround for a 90-day extract of role_changes and policy_updates? Prefer CSV or compressed JSON.

Attachments: sample from our end (see attached) for expected columns.

Thanks,
Amir Patel
Security Ops — HealthNode
[Attachment: requested_columns_example.csv (CSV, 3KB)]
message_2_subject: Re: AuthZ change log retention and extract plan for SOC 2 / SIG review
message_2_body:
Amir — thanks for the callout. Quick answers up-front:

- Logged events: role.grant, role.revoke, role.modify (name/description), policy.created, policy.updated, policy.applied, admin.login, admin.api_key.create/delete. Each event has actor_id, actor_email, target_id, target_type, before/after delta (when applicable), timestamp (UTC), request_id, and service_region.
- Retention: default 13 months for admin/authz events (configurable for Dedicated/Private customers), 90 days hot, remainder archived with indexed manifests.
- Export: we can produce a signed CSV export or compressed newline-delimited JSON with a manifest file and SHA256 checksums. Typical turnaround for a 90-day slice is 24–48 business hours for hosted accounts; expedited 8–12 hours for enterprise SLA.

I’ve looped in Kimberly and Neha to confirm the exact manifest schema and to schedule the export. Can you confirm the timezone window you want us to use (UTC vs PST) and whether you need redaction of any PII fields (actor_email) in the delivered extract?

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: authz_change_log_sample.csv (CSV, 12KB)]
message_3_subject: Re: AuthZ change log retention and extract plan for SOC 2 / SIG review
message_3_body:
Amir — hi, Kimberly here from Compliance Ops.

We’ll deliver:
- Package: export.tar.gz containing data.csv (or ndjson), manifest.yaml, checksums.txt, and a small readme.md describing fields and any redaction applied.
- Schema highlights: actor_id (uuid), actor_role, actor_email, event_type, event_subtype, target_id, target_type, delta_before, delta_after, request_id, timestamp_utc, region, retention_tier.
- Redaction options: we can redact actor_email and replace with hashed_email if you select that option; note that redaction will affect mapping back to user accounts in your mapping step.
- Delivery: secure S3 presigned URL (expiry 72 hours) or SFTP push to HealthNode. Also can provide a signed manifest and PGP-encrypted bundle on request.

For your SIG: we typically include a 90-day sample and a 13-month retention summary CSV that indicates which events fall into hot vs archived storage. If you confirm UTC window (we recommend UTC) and whether you want PII redacted, we’ll schedule the export for tomorrow and aim for the 24–48 hour turnaround.

Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: export_manifest_template.yaml (YAML, 2KB)]
message_4_subject: Re: AuthZ change log retention and extract plan for SOC 2 / SIG review
message_4_body:
Thanks — that all looks good. We’ll take the UTC window and request actor_email hashed (SHA256) for the delivered extract. Delivery via S3 presigned URL is fine — please include the signed manifest.

Two quick clarifications before you run it: 1) please include the earliest event timestamp in the manifest for the slice, and 2) include the query used to generate the slice (so our auditors can reproduce).

If you can confirm those two items and kick off an export tomorrow morning, we’ll mark the SIG submission as on track.

Best,
Amir
Security Ops — HealthNode
